destinations.post_study_work_summary: Bachelor's and master's graduates on a Student visa may apply in the UK for the Graduate visa: two years if applying by 31 December 2026, or 18 months if applying on or after 1 January 2027.

F-1 graduates may usually receive up to 12 months of post-completion Optional Practical Training per higher education level. Graduates with qualifying STEM degrees may apply for a further 24-month STEM OPT extension.

Degree graduates (Level 7 or above, 30 weeks' full-time study in New Zealand) may receive a Post-Study Work Visa of up to three years. From 16 November 2026, Level 7 graduate diploma holders with a bachelor's degree also qualify.

The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, usually allows graduates to stay between two and three years depending on their qualification. Applicants must generally be aged 35 or under, with exceptions.

Eligible graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit. Master's programmes of at least eight months, and other programmes of two years or more, may lead to a three-year permit. Most applicants have needed language results since 1 November 2024.
International graduates of German universities may receive a residence permit of up to 18 months to seek qualified employment, during which any type of work is permitted. The permit is not renewable.
